summary: Architects of Nova is a free co-op Roblox game for 1-4 players aged 6-12 where kids design, build, launch and fly real space missions. A solar superstorm has silenced every colony, and the cadets of the Citadel must restore contact across seven chapters: a CubeSat, an orbital relay network, ice prospecting at the Moon's south pole, a Mars landing, a Webb-like telescope at L2, Europa, and an asteroid deflection inspired by DART. Every mission is a full engineering loop: the team votes on the objective, assembles a spacecraft from real subsystems while balancing mass, power, data, communications and budget, passes a GO/NO-GO launch readiness poll that explains every problem before liftoff, runs mission operations, flies a crew to two landing sites with rovers, and gets a debrief with a NASA lesson and a quiz. Live NASA DONKI and NeoWs data drive the solar storms and asteroid alerts. Four roles (Commander, Engineer, Scientist, Comms) make every player essential, turning abstract mission trade-offs into hands-on, collaborative play in Russian and English.
details:
What it does: Architects of Nova turns the challenge, designing a whole space mission from concept to operations, into a cooperative Roblox adventure for kids aged 6-12. Up to four friends join a crew at the Citadel, a colony base whose satellites were burned out by a solar superstorm. Seven story chapters each ask for a different mission: a 3U CubeSat, a communications network (one big GEO satellite or a low-orbit swarm), a lunar south-pole ice prospector, a Mars lander, a folding-mirror telescope at L2, a Europa probe and a DART-style asteroid deflection.

How it works: every mission follows the real NASA flow. A hologram briefing ends with a team vote shown as visual cards with 3D previews and pros and cons. In the hangar the crew assembles the spacecraft from 25 real-world parts (flight computers, batteries, an RTG, solar panels, antennas, instruments, a radiation vault, landing systems) into dedicated slots while live gauges track mass, power, data, communications, budget and time. Players pick a rocket and an orbit, rehearse at mission control and must pass a GO/NO-GO launch readiness poll that names each problem and how to fix it before launch, so failures teach instead of punish. After launch the crew runs operations at four role consoles, suits up, flies to two landing sites per world, drives four-seat rovers, repairs systems through short mini-games and returns for a flight report with a NASA lesson and a quiz.

Learning and impact: the Parts Book (25 parts and 4 rockets with real NASA examples), the Rocket Lab (stack stages using thrust-to-weight and the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation: one stage reaches about 6 km/s, orbit needs about 9 km/s) and a NASA mission file for every chapter ground each choice in real science. Live NASA DONKI solar-flare data sets the storm level and emergency pacing, and NeoWs near-Earth asteroid data fills the threat board. The game is free, bilingual (Russian and English), kid-safe (credits are only earned, no loot boxes or paid boosts) and runs on PC, tablet and phone.

Tools and creativity: Roblox Studio and Luau with a server-authoritative architecture (mission, hangar, expedition, emergency, rover and progress services), custom client UI and cinematics, Roblox DataStore profiles, Roblox Studio AI generation for some 3D meshes and materials, and a three.js website for the presentation. The project is creative through an original space-opera story with a mentor hologram, a rival admiral and a helper drone; co-op roles where every player matters (Commander, Engineer, Scientist, Comms); a cinematic opening of the solar storm; and visual votes so even the youngest players understand each trade-off.
dataRefs: NASA Open APIs - DONKI solar flares (live data in the game)
NASA Open APIs - Asteroids NeoWs near-Earth objects (live data in the game)
NASA CubeSat 101 (CubeSat sizes, mass and margin rules)
NASA Glenn - Beginner's Guide to Rockets (thrust, rocket equation, staging)
Mars 2020 Perseverance (signal delay, landing sequence, sample tubes)
James Webb Space Telescope (folding mirror, sunshield, L2)
Europa Clipper (1/r2 sunlight, radiation, ice-penetrating radar)
DART - Double Asteroid Redirection Test (kinetic impact)
LCROSS (water ice in permanently shadowed craters)
Juno (radiation vault, solar arrays at Jupiter)
projectRefs: Roblox Studio and Creator Hub (game engine, Luau, Roblox AI 3D mesh and material generation)
Roblox audio library: APM Music and Pro Sound Effects licensed for Roblox experiences
Google Fonts: Barlow Condensed and Inter (presentation website)
Claude by Anthropic (AI assistant used for code, text and translation)
